clue.text: Negligible snub

definitions.meaning: so small as not to matter
to ignore or insult someone pointedly

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: an adjective for tiny or trivial, and a verb for treating someone with disdain.

clue.text: One so intoxicated, a whiskey nearly finished

parts.note: taken as written
lit is slang for drunk

indicators.note: nearly finished says the word loses its final letter before it is complete

parts.note: rye is a North American whiskey

explanation.surface: A lone drinker gets drunk while a bottle of whiskey runs almost dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly finished' trims the last letter from RYE, leaving RY. 'One' looks like a pronoun for the drinker but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary is a single person living alone, a recluse, so one on their own.

clue.text: Mandarin peel from corridor and apricot behind chest of drawers

indicators.note: the peeled pieces come behind, that is after, the chest of drawers in the answer

parts.note: a bureau is a chest of drawers or writing desk

indicators.note: peel suggests the skin, so only the outside letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Someone has dropped fruit peel behind the furniture in a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peel from' takes the outer letters CR and AT from 'corridor' and 'apricot'. 'Mandarin' suggests the citrus fruit beside the apricot and peel, but it means an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a senior official in a bureaucracy, especially the civil service; the word comes from imperial China.

clue.text: Lift jug

definitions.meaning: to lift is slang for to steal
jug is old slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang: nick means steal (lift) and also a prison or police station (jug).

clue.text: Huge city in Ghana is built around front of harbour

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single letter
built suggests the letters are put together into a new structure
front of takes the first letter of the word harbour

explanation.surface: A large city in Ghana has grown up around its harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' makes SANGHAI, and 'around' sets the harbour's first letter inside it after the S; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai, in China, is one of the most populous cities in the world.

clue.text: Twin, one using the phone

definitions.meaning: a dead ... is an exact double or lookalike
someone who rings a number is literally a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A ringer is a lookalike, as in dead ringer, and jokingly also anyone who rings someone up.

clue.text: Sparkling drink recalled in special occasion

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink is remembered from a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters hidden across 'special occasion', ALOC, which 'recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a carbonated soft drink, so a sparkling one.

clue.text: Just out of the oven, pork pie eaten by the Queen, as accommodating type?

parts.note: freshly baked food is hot

indicators.note: eaten by means the word goes inside the other, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie

explanation.surface: A hot pork pie is being eaten by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is British rhyming slang for a fib. 'eaten by' makes ELIER, the fib inside the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs a hotel and so provides accommodation for guests; the question mark marks the playful description.

clue.text: Monster that's meaner welcomed by not very many in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the whole combination is read backwards
welcomed by means the word is taken inside the other

parts.note: few means not very many
lower can mean meaner or baser

explanation.surface: A nastier creature is let in by a small group as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' gives FLOWEREW and 'in retreat' turns that whole string backwards, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a monster of folklore, a man who turns into a wolf.

clue.text: Religious writer Thomas Oliver's request

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas ..., the Catholic martyr and author of Utopia
Oliver Twist famously asks the workhouse master for a second helping

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More wrote religious works, and Dickens's orphan Oliver Twist asks for more gruel.

clue.text: Smart boy's heart in strong beer

parts.note: to smart and to sting both mean to hurt sharply

indicators.note: heart takes the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A clever lad has a heart for powerful ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle letter O of 'boy's'. 'Smart' looks like an adjective for the boy but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old British name for a strong ale or beer.

clue.text: Happen again to take in Omani capital, aside from seaside resort

indicators.note: to take in means the word receives another piece inside it

parts.note: to recur is to happen again

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word
aside from tells us to remove the letters of aside from the word seaside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something happens again in Oman's capital, away from the beach town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' and 'from' are the indicators. 'seaside resort' looks like one phrase, but 'resort' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recourse to something is to resort to it; both nouns mean a source of help turned to.

clue.text: Name for a whisky cocktail about right for brandy

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the inner letter

parts.note: a whisky mac is whisky mixed with ginger wine

explanation.surface: Someone names a whisky cocktail suitable for brandy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: A whisky mac is a British drink of Scotch and ginger wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a brandy distilled from the skins and pips left after grapes are pressed for wine.

clue.text: Last daring manoeuvres in battle

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters are moved around like troops

explanation.surface: A final bold military operation takes place in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' looks like part of the war story but rearranges LAST DARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad was the 1942-43 Second World War battle in which the Soviet army defeated the German Sixth Army.

clue.text: Pure delusion that's dystopian

indicators.note: dystopian suggests something gone badly wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A pure fantasy is revealed as grimly dystopian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dystopian' rearranges DELUSION; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsoiled means clean and unstained, which is to say pure.

clue.text: Conference Centre not used by Herb

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is not used, so it is dropped

parts.note: parsley is a common garden herb

explanation.surface: A conference centre is not being used by a man named Herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre not used by' drops S, the middle letter of PARSLEY. 'Herb' looks like a man's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A parley is a conference or discussion, especially between enemies to agree terms.

clue.text: See, that's revolting Irish water

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ugh is the exclamation for something revolting

explanation.surface: Look, that disgusting stuff is Irish water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb or a bishop's see, but stands for the old interjection LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lough is the Irish word for a lake or sea inlet, the counterpart of the Scottish loch.

clue.text: Author eating funny fruit

indicators.note: eating means the outer word takes the other inside it

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
a funny can mean a joke, as does gag

explanation.surface: A writer is eating a peculiar fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts GAG inside GREENE. 'funny' looks like an adjective describing the fruit but stands for a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a green variety of plum.

clue.text: After conclusion of whodunnit, anything explained?

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer
conclusion of takes the final letter of the word

parts.note: aught is an old word meaning anything

explanation.surface: At the end of a detective story, has everything been explained?
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion of' takes T from 'whodunnit'; 'After' puts AUGHT after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taught means instructed, with things made clear, so explained in the sense of shown or told.

clue.text: Hand placed on rugby player in routine

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a straight is a hand in poker
a forward is a rugby player in the scrum

explanation.surface: A hand is placed on a rugby player during a set routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' looks like a body part touching the player, but it is a poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Straightforward means simple and uncomplicated, as a routine task is.

clue.text: Lost a letter, I learned

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and are out of order

explanation.surface: Someone lost a letter, and that is how they found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' rearranges A LETTER I; 'learned' looks like a verb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means well read and educated, which is learned as an adjective.

clue.text: All fingers and thumbs maybe working for joint

parts.note: two hands have ten digits in total
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A clumsy person is supposedly working on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All fingers and thumbs' is an idiom for clumsy, but here it simply counts digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting end in a mortise and tenon woodworking joint.

clue.text: Big noise, always, as criminal

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Constant loud din is treated as criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is a poetic form of ever; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a criminal running an illegal business such as extortion.

clue.text: Frank taking fall — exercise too much?

parts.note: overt means open or frank
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: An honest man takes a tumble, perhaps from working out too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name and 'fall' like a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to train excessively, so to exercise too much.

clue.text: Cross about Polish maiden lifting cheese

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the rest

parts.note: a liger is the cross between a lion and a tigress

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting reads the pieces upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to polish is to rub
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An angry Polish girl is picking up some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' gives MBUR and 'about' wraps the big-cat hybrid round it. 'Cross' looks like angry and 'Polish' like the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a strong-smelling soft cheese from the Limburg region of Belgium and the Netherlands.

clue.text: Great waste to invest in the stuff of mine?

indicators.note: to invest in means to put the word inside the other

parts.note: coal is what comes out of a mine
a loss is wastage or something wasted

explanation.surface: Is it a big waste to put money into the mining business?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to invest in' looks financial but means place inside, the mining surface hiding the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means huge, which is one sense of great.

clue.text: Under top of skirt, fold cut back

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece sits under the first
top of takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: to crimp is to press into small folds

explanation.surface: A fold is cut back under the waistband of a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' takes S from 'skirt' and 'Under' puts CRIMP below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise, to cut back on spending.

clue.text: Chip in every last piece of Dresden china tragic? Oh no!

indicators.note: every last piece of takes the final letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A chip in precious Dresden porcelain is a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chip' sounds like damage to the china, but it is a tortilla chip; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served with melted cheese.

clue.text: Bar stocking old wine

indicators.note: stocking means the word holds the other inside it

parts.note: bar and save can both mean except

explanation.surface: A bar is stocking an old wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub but means except, as SAVE does.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto region of Italy.
